newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh pipeline opens to tackle power crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh pipeline opens to tackle power crisis.

text.p: A pipeline has begun carrying gas to a power plant in southeastern Bangladesh to help reduce a crippling electricity shortage, officials said on Saturday.
Energy ministry officials said the 58-km (36-mile) Ashuganj-Bakhrabad gas pipeline began a test run on Friday night and was expected to formally open for full-scale operation in the next few days.

The 210-megawatt power plant at Raojan, near the southeastern port city of Chittagong, has remained idle for about two years due to supply problems at nearby Bakhrabad gas field. Officials said it would soon generate electricity.
"Refuelling of Raojan plant will greatly reduce the gap in generation and supply (of electricity)," one official said.
Bangladesh has suffered a severe electricity shortage because of dwindling gas supplies and ageing power plants.
The country currently produces a maximum 1,700 megawatts against a demand of 2,100 megwatts, resulting in frequent outages at homes and factories.
Last year, Bangladesh opened power generation to the private sector, drawing inquiries from more than dozen foreign firms.
Bangladesh has proven gas reserves of 10 trillion cubic feet.
